narrative: Material PL2__ME04FCDD exhibits smooth continuous demand averaging 240.9 units/day with a CV of 0.65 and a statistically significant downward trend over the observation period. Lead times are very short on average (0.27 days) but highly variable (CV=1.40), making lead-time variance the dominant driver of safety stock requirements. An (r,Q) policy with EOQ-derived batch size of 2,146 units and safety stock of 201 units meets the 95% service level while reducing total annual inventory cost by 91.7% compared to the current MOQ-based approach.
warnings: Order quantity (2146) nearly exhausts available storage capacity after safety stock (201); remaining headroom is ~0.2 units — monitor any upward safety-stock revision.
Significant downward demand trend detected (p<0.05); mean demand estimate should be reviewed quarterly.

research_insights.selection_rationale: Smooth continuous demand (non-zero fraction 93.8%, CV 0.65) with very short but variable lead times is well-served by a continuous-review (r,Q) policy. EOQ batching eliminates the excessive ordering frequency caused by the current 166-unit MOQ policy and captures the dominant holding-vs-ordering cost trade-off efficiently.
research_insights.boundary_risk: The recommended order quantity of 2,146 units combined with safety stock of 201 units reaches 2,347 units, consuming virtually all 2,347.211 units of storage capacity. Any increase in safety stock due to demand variability changes will require a proportional reduction in order quantity, potentially increasing ordering frequency and cost.
